words_to_read_new.meaning: in- means in + JECT means throw: to throw in, to force in
e- means out + JECT means throw: to throw out
re- means back + JECT means throw: to throw back, to refuse
pro- means forward + JECT means throw + -or means a thing that: a thing that throws a picture forward
inter- means between + JECT means throw: to throw words in between
ad- means to + JECT means throw + -ive means relating to: a word thrown next to a noun
in- means in + JECT means throw + -ion means the act of: the act of throwing medicine in
re- means back + JECT means throw + -ion means the act of: the act of throwing back
ob- means against + JECT means throw + -ion means the act of: the act of throwing a protest against

associated_word_exceptions.reason: Ground 3: pro + ject + -or is the clearest thing-that-throws word in the family and the one students see every day; the card lists projection and projectile but no -or word.
associated_word_exceptions.source: Macquarie Dictionary: projector, an apparatus for throwing an image on a screen.

sessions.wtr_new_notes:
SAY: "Learn ject once and you can read a whole family of words about throwing."
READ each word as it appears, say what it means, then link ject to the card meaning: throw.
inject - in means in + JECT means throw: to throw in. A nurse injects medicine into your arm.
eject - e means out + JECT means throw: to throw out. Press the button to eject the disc.
reject - re means back + JECT means throw: to throw back. Fishers reject small fish and throw them back.
projector - pro means forward + JECT means throw + or means a thing that: it throws the picture forward onto the screen.
interject - inter means between + JECT means throw: to throw words in between. Please don't interject while I'm talking.
adjective - ad means to + JECT means throw + ive means relating to: a word thrown next to a noun. In red car, red is the adjective.
injection - the act of throwing in. The vet gave our dog an injection.
rejection - the act of throwing back. The editor sent the writer a rejection letter.
objection - ob means against: the act of throwing a protest against. The lawyer shouted, "Objection!"

grammar.header_notes:
PURPOSE: A semicolon joins two full sentences that belong together. It can take the place of and, but or so.
WHY THIS WEEK: last week we linked argument sentences with connectives. A semicolon is a tighter link, with no joining word at all.
TIME: 5 minutes, no more - I do 1 min, We do 1 question, You do 3 questions at about 30 seconds each. One question per slide; your click reveals the answer.
ROUTINE: all grammar is written in the OG book. No boards - books, fingers and voices only.
PREP: test both sides - each must make sense as a full sentence on its own. If one side cannot stand alone, no semicolon.

i_do.title: Swap the joining word for a semicolon
i_do.rule: A semicolon joins two full sentences. It replaces and, but or so.
i_do.example:
The ref rejected the goal, and fans booed.
The ref rejected the goal; fans booed.
items: Both sides must make sense on their own.
i_do.footer: Your turn: what goes in the gap?
i_do.notes:
ANSWER: The ref rejected the goal; fans booed.
1. SAY: "A semicolon is a dot on top of a comma. It joins two full sentences that belong together, and it takes the place of the joining word."
2. WRITE: copy the first sentence on the class board. CROSS OUT the comma and and. WRITE the semicolon in their place.
3. ASK: "Can each side stand alone as a full sentence? Thumbs up or down, voices off." 5 sec. EXPECT: thumbs up.
TRAP: a capital after the semicolon. Fix: it is still one sentence, so the second part starts with a small letter; student fixes the f.
---
Purpose: one grammar block a week - model the semicolon replacing a conjunction. [I Do | Explicit modelling | Grammar | HITS 3]
PREP: rejected is this week's ject word in action.

we_do.title: What goes in the gap?
we_do.rule: Pick what joins the two full sentences.

round.prompt: We packed the car ___ we drove to the beach.
round.why: two full sentences, no joining word
round.notes:
ANSWER: 2 - a semicolon. We packed the car; we drove to the beach.
1. SAY: "Read it in your head. Two full sentences, no joining word. What goes in the gap?"
2. ASK: "One finger comma, two semicolon, three both, voices off, show me on three." 5 sec. EXPECT: two fingers.
3. REVEAL after fingers are scanned. ASK: "How do you know?" Cold call one student. EXPECT: both sides are full sentences and there is no and.
TRAP: choosing 3. Fix: the semicolon replaces and - you never need both. Student votes again.
CLARIFY: a comma alone cannot join two full sentences; it needs a joining word, or swap it for a semicolon.
---
Purpose: guided check - spot both rules at once. [We Do | Guided practice | Grammar | HITS 7]

you_do.title: Swap in a semicolon
you_do.rule: Write the sentence with a semicolon instead of the joining word.

TRAP: keeping so after the semicolon. Fix: the semicolon replaces it; student crosses so out.
EXTENSION: Two in one - write one semicolon sentence that uses two of this week's ject words.
HELP: give the start, It started to rain;, and let them finish it.

EXPECT: adjective.
4. ASK: "Which word means easy to carry?"
10 sec, turn and talk. Then: "Everyone, together, on three."
EXPECT: portable.

subblocks.heading: Swap in a semicolon
subblocks.instruction: Rewrite each sentence. Use a semicolon instead of the comma and the joining word.
example: It was cold, so we lit the fire.  ->  It was cold; we lit the fire.

items: The bell rang, so we packed up our books.
My sister loves netball, but I would rather play soccer.

answers: The bell rang; we packed up our books.
My sister loves netball; I would rather play soccer.

subblocks.heading: Your own semicolon
subblocks.instruction: Join two full sentences about our school camp with a semicolon.
answers: e.g. The cabins were tiny; we still slept well. (Both sides must make sense alone.)

subblocks.heading: Which job does the suffix give?
subblocks.instruction: Try each word in the frames. Write its job: noun, verb or adjective.
tip: the ___ = noun      to ___ = verb      very ___ = adjective      e.g. gravity: the gravity = noun

subblocks.heading: Complete the sentence
subblocks.instruction: Write the learned word that fits each gap. Spell it carefully.

items: Our family pays the ___ on our house every month.
The new headphones came with a two-year ___.

subblocks.heading: ject = throw
subblocks.instruction: Break each word into its parts, then write what the parts mean. Use the parts box.
example: rejection = re + ject + ion = back + throw + the act of
answers: projector = pro + ject + or = forward + throw + a thing that
interjection = inter + ject + ion = between + throw + the act of
adjective = ad + ject + ive = to + throw + relating to

subblocks.heading: ject = throw: new words
subblocks.instruction: These words were not on our lists. Use the parts to work out what each one means.

items: ejector = e (out) + ject + or (a thing that) =
injector = in (in) + ject + or (a thing that) =

answers: ejector: a thing that throws something out (like an ejector seat)
injector: a thing that throws something in (like a fuel injector)

dictation.sentence: The nurse gave me an injection, and I did not even flinch.
chunks: The nurse gave me an injection,

punctuation: comma before and (it joins two full sentences)

dictation.sentence: Our class projector broke; the shop replaced it under the guarantee.

follow_up.question: Part A, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: the comma or the joining word kept in either sentence
follow_up.next_move: In next week's dictation, read a sentence with , so and ask the class to swap in a semicolon on whiteboards.

follow_up.question: Part A, Q2
follow_up.flag_when: one side of the semicolon cannot stand alone
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Read Review, say "The bell rang; packed up" and ask which side is not a full sentence.

follow_up.question: Part B, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: 2 or more of the 6 jobs wrong
follow_up.next_move: During the review cards, stop on -ive and ask the class to try active in the/to/very frames.

follow_up.question: Part C, Q1
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Spell Review, add "mortgage" on the class whiteboard and ask which letter is silent.

follow_up.question: Part D, Q1
follow_up.flag_when: ject = throw missing, or 2 of the 3 sums wrong
follow_up.next_move: During the review cards, stop on ject and ask for two ject words and what each part means.

follow_up.question: Part D, Q2
follow_up.flag_when: a meaning that ignores ject (throw) or the printed part
follow_up.next_move: During Words to Read Review, add "ejector" on the class whiteboard and ask what it throws and which way.

follow_up.question: Part E
follow_up.flag_when: 3 or more COPS points lost across the two sentences
follow_up.next_move: In next week's dictation, stop after the CHECK step and have the student redo their weakest COPS letter aloud with you.
